marble.name: Adding and subtracting mixed numbers
marble.subject: Mathematics
marble.description: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators, including by converting to improper fractions or using properties of operations
marble.prompt: If a recipe calls for 1 and 2/5 cups of oats and another batch needs 2 and 3/5 cups, can you add them together to get the total — including converting when the fifths add up past a whole?

cluster.summary: Your child is discovering their first fractions — learning to recognise and name halves and quarters as equal parts of shapes, objects, and groups.

misconceptions: Adds across the fraction parts (3/5 + 4/5 → 7/10), applying whole-number addition to numerator and denominator
Subtracts smaller-from-larger in each column and never borrows (4 2/6 − 1 5/6 → 3 3/6, taking |2−5|=3)
Leaves an improper fraction part in the answer (3 7/5) instead of regrouping to 4 2/5
Miscounts when converting mixed to improper (2 3/5 → 10/5 then forgets the +3/5, or writes 5/5)
representations: Number line: jump the whole numbers, then the fraction parts, crossing whole boundaries
Bar model with whole tiles plus fraction tiles; a whole tile that shatters into b unit-fractions for the borrow, or b fraction tiles that fuse into a whole
The regroup written as 4 = 3 + 6/6 (or the improper rewrite 26/6)
Improper-fraction form beside the mixed form for comparison

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Answer 3 3/6 (or 3 1/2); the working shows 5/6−2/6 with no exchange of a whole
wrongAnswers.fix: Make the exchange physical — trade one whole for 6/6 so there are 8 sixths to subtract from — or switch to improper fractions (26/6 − 11/6), which removes the borrow altogether

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: The fraction part of the sum has a changed denominator (7/10 rather than 7/5); the whole numbers may be added correctly
wrongAnswers.fix: Return to fifths as a fixed unit — three fifths and four fifths is seven fifths — on a locked bar; re-establish joining same-size parts before regrouping

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Answer written as 3 7/5 (numerator ≥ denominator in a mixed number); the addition itself is sound
wrongAnswers.fix: Scaffold, don't reteach — prompt 'is 7/5 more than a whole? then tidy it into the whole-number part'; the child already added correctly
